full_judgment:
8. Mr MA Karim submits that the appellate Court below has committed an error of law resulting in a miscarriage of justice by failing to consider the true import of and the weight to be attached to an admit card issued by an Education Board. He has referred to an unreported decision of a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 743 of 1980 (Judgment on 5-5-81) and the appeal, preferred therefrom in an unreported decision of the Appellate Division in CPS LA No. 200 of 1981 (Judgment on 29-5-81) in which the Appellate Division has held that the Matriculation Certificate is the most reliable document recording a person's age. The High Court Division also held the same. Mr. Karim also referred to the case of Imam Hossain Bepari-vs-Election Tribunal, 31 DLR 381, wherein it has been observed that SSC Certificate is the most authentic proof of age. Those cases were of course decided in the light of the total evidence on age. 

 13. I have closely examined the pleadings, the evidence and the judgment of the Tribunal in the matter of 412 votes alleged to be the votes of dead and absentee voters. It is true that the petitioner has given the names, ages, addresses, father's names, etc. of all the 23 dead voters and 389 absentee voters in his application. It is also true that the opposite party No. 1 did not specifically deny that those were dead or absentee voters. At the trial the petitioner filed the same list of dead and absentee voters (Exhibit 1) duly certified by one Mr Mafizul Hoque, Chairman of the concerned Union Parishad. The Tribunal held that the petitioner by listing the names of the dead and absentee voters in his election petition and by producing Exhibit 1 has discharged his burden of proof as to the number of dead and absentee voters of Ward No 3. This finding, not being a correct one on the law of burden of proof, cannot be accepted. 

 14. When the petitioner alleges that some particular voters were dead and absent on the date of election on 6-3-84, he takes upon himself the burden of so proving. If he gives a list of dead and absentee voters and the opposite party cannot or does not controvert the same, the contents of the list are not proved. It is not the opposite party No. 1 who maintains officially a list of dead and absentee voters. He does not have a special knowledge as to who are dead and absentee voters. 

 15. That special knowledge can only be claimed by those who are in charge of preparation and finalisation of voters list and are also in charge of continuous correction thereof. It is they who are competent to say whether there were any dead or absentee voters in Ward No. 3 on the day of election. Even they may not be fully conversant' as to which particular voters were absent from the polling centre on the day of election. So it comes to this that the petitioner has to prove in each and every case, by adducing evidence, that a particular votter absented himself from the polls on the date of election, even though his/her name was validly entered in the voters list Mere listing of dead and absentee persons and mere production of a list certified by a person who does not officially maintain the voters' list are not good enough to discharge the prima facie burden. PWs. 2-5 have specifically named some of their relations who were dead or absent on the date of poll and whose names occur in the list given by the petitioner. At best the petitioner, has proved the death of those voters who have been specifically named by PWs 2-5, because there is no evidence in rebuttal, but with regard to the other persons, a general statement that they were dead or absent without giving specific evidence to that effect, is of no assistance to the petitioner. The death of a few voters specifically named does not alter the electoral picture.
